claims.claim: Version control records changes to files over time so specific earlier versions can be recalled.
Git models committed project state as snapshots and many ordinary operations can use local repository data.
The working tree is the checked-out project copy; the staging area or index stores selected content for the next commit.
A normal git commit creates a commit from the current index and a log message, while git add incrementally adds file changes to the index.
A commit has a directory tree, parent commit IDs, author and committer information, and a commit message.
A branch refers to the latest commit on that branch, and a new commit updates the current branch to point to it.
